title: Dilucidationes super methodo elegantissima, qua illustris de la Grange usus est in integranda aequatione differentiali dx/√X = dy/√Y

deep.reconstruction:
Context: In E506 Euler explains Lagrange's method of integrating dx/√X = dy/√Y, where X and Y are the same quartic in x and in y. The method gives the first integral (√X − √Y)/(x−y) = √(Δ + D(x+y) + E(x+y)²), with Δ an arbitrary constant. In §59 Euler notes a 'paradox': this formula breaks down when X and Y are perfect squares. That case is dx/R = dy/S with R = a+bx+cx², S = a+by+cy², whose integral is logarithmic or arctangent rather than elliptic. It is not a 0/0 or ∞−∞ case.

To resolve it he regularises. Put X = R²+α and Y = S²+α with α infinitesimal. Then A = a²+α, B = 2ab, C = 2ac+b², D = 2bc, E = c², and √X ≈ R+α/(2R).

This page: since (R−S)/(x−y) = b+cp with p = x+y, the integral becomes (b+cp)(1−α/(2RS)) = √(Δ+2bcp+c²p²). Squaring and keeping terms to first order in α gives b² − α(b+cp)²/(RS) = Δ.

At α = 0 this would force Δ = b², so the arbitrary constant disappears; that is the paradox. The cure is to let Δ differ from b² infinitesimally: Δ = b² − αΓ. This yields the finite relation (b+c(x+y))² = Γ(a+bx+cx²)(a+by+cy²).

§63 simplifies this. Set F = RS/(cp+b)² (constant) and u = xy. Expanding, RS = a² + abp + ac(p²−2u) + b²u + bcpu + c²u². The next page completes the reduction by division: RS = (cp+b)(ap+bu) + (a−cu)². Hence F = a/c − (b/c)V + V² with V = (a−cxy)/(b+c(x+y)). So V must be constant, which is the algebraic integral of dx/R = dy/S. It is a bilinear-symmetric (Möbius-type) relation between x and y: the degenerate, rational addition law.
errors: In §63 the printed fraction RS/(b−cp)² should read RS/(b+cp)²; the next line correctly uses F(cp+b)². This is a misprint, not a mathematical error.
The truncation 'higher powers of α omitted' is legitimate. The squared equation is exact to O(α), and the O(α²) term is consistently dropped once Δ = b² − αΓ.
All algebra on the page checks out: √X−√Y = (R−S)(1−α/(2RS)) + O(α²), the squaring step, and the expansion of RS in p and u.

ideas.what: Resolving a degenerate case of a general integral formula by an infinitesimal perturbation (X = R²+α), with the arbitrary constant also perturbed (Δ = b²−αΓ) so that it survives the limit
ideas.modern_name: Regularisation / singular limit of a one-parameter family of first integrals; first-order perturbation
ideas.usually_credited_to: General limiting technique, standard in 18th-century analysis (Euler, Lagrange)
ideas.where_published: E506, Acta Acad. Sci. Petrop. 1778 (pub. 1781); Opera omnia I.21

ideas.what: Degeneration of Lagrange's elliptic addition integral to the case of square X, Y, giving (b+c(x+y))² = Γ RS and finally (a−cxy)/(b+c(x+y)) = const
ideas.modern_name: Degeneration of the elliptic-curve addition law to a singular (rational) curve: multiplicative or additive group law, Möbius/tangent-type addition
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (addition theorems for ∫dx/(a+bx+cx²)); the modern singular-cubic viewpoint is 19th–20th century
ideas.where_published: E506; related addition forms in Euler's earlier papers on dx/√X = dy/√Y (e.g. E251, E261)

ideas.what: Identity RS = (cp+b)(ap+bu) + (a−cu)² with p = x+y, u = xy, used to reduce the integral to a single invariant V

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but routine treatment of a degenerate case. The result, the rational addition law for ∫dx/(a+bx+cx²), is classical, and the perturbative resolution of the 'paradox' is published in E506 itself and in the Opera omnia. Nothing appears to be absent from the record.
transcription_corrections: Page header ') 48 (' is omitted from the transcription.
The transcription faithfully reproduces the printed misprint 'RS/(b−cp)²' in §63; the intended reading is RS/(b+cp)².
In the §61 continuation the radicand is printed as Δ + 2bcp + ccpp, matching the transcription.
